speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mononeuritis Multiplex secondary to Polyarteritis Nodosa (PAN).

I have identified key risk factors including heavy smoking, alcohol use, anabolic steroid use, and significant weight loss alongside your arm weakness. These suggest an underlying vasculitis rather than simple compression. REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, ANCA panel, and Hepatitis B surface antigen. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical Spine and Right Arm.
